brand.name: TrailFold
brand.positioning: Practical lightweight bags for commuters who take short weekend trips; restrained, useful, plain-spoken voice.

policies.shipping: Free US shipping; delivery estimate 4-7 business days
policies.returns: 30-day returns for unused products; return shipping paid by customer
policies.discounts: No current discount. Any new discount needs owner approval.

claim_constraints: No evidence for waterproof, medical, sustainability or lifetime-durability claims.
No clinical or controlled product test results.

themes: customers ask whether a 15-inch laptop fits
customers ask whether rain protection means waterproof
customer_themes.note: Themes, not verbatim licensed testimonials; no fabricated quotes or endorsements.

website_snapshot.pdp_details: Laptop sizing and delivery window are below reviews; CTA says Buy now. No field speed or session-recording data.

shopify.definitions: Revenue excludes tax/shipping; periods equal length. Funnel counts are session-based and internally consistent, but no controlled attribution experiment.

meta.settings: 7-day click plus 1-day view; no incremental lift study. Meta reported value not reconciled to Shopify orders.

creative_history.name: Desk-to-trail demonstration
creative_history.observed_result: Largest spend recipient; mature creative. No asset-level contribution data.

creative_history.name: Laptop-fit comparison
creative_history.observed_result: Higher CTR in small test; conversion sample not supplied.

flows.name: checkout abandonment
flows.observed_gap: No Added to Cart flow; filters not audited.

klaviyo.note: Revenue attribution overlaps other systems; no holdout or recent deliverability audit.

resources.cash_constraint: Protect replenishment payments; no additional inventory purchase approved.

tasks.title: Diagnose conversion decline
tasks.request: Why has conversion fallen? Calculate overall and device rates, locate the likely funnel problem, distinguish evidence from hypotheses, and identify the three most useful missing facts.
criteria: Overall 3% to 2%; mobile 2.667% to 1.5%; desktop stays 4%.
Add-to-cart rate 10% to 8%; checkout completion remains 50%.
Do not assert speed, tracking failure or creative fatigue as proven cause.

tasks.title: Reconcile attribution
tasks.request: Meta ROAS improved: should we raise spending? Reconcile this with Shopify and Klaviyo and explain what can and cannot be concluded.
criteria: Meta ROAS 3 to 3.2 while Shopify revenue/spend falls 3 to about 2.045.
Do not add Meta and email attributed revenue or call either incremental.
Require order/window reconciliation and contribution before scaling.

tasks.title: Discount unit economics
tasks.request: For one Daypack order, compare full price with a proposed 20% discount at $30 CAC. Use only the listed item costs, shipping and fees; no other products or lifetime value. Calculate pre-ad contribution, after-ad contribution and break-even ROAS. Should we use this offer?
criteria: Full price pre-ad 39.60, after-ad 9.60, break-even ROAS about 2.02.
Discount price 64, pre-ad 24.08, after-ad -5.92, break-even ROAS about 2.66.
Do not treat a discount as automatically profitable or rely on unknown LTV.

tasks.title: Diagnose creative fatigue
tasks.request: Are the Meta ads fatigued? Explain the evidence, compute implied link CPC from CPM and CTR, and suggest a discriminating next check.
criteria: CPC rises from 0.80 to 1.25.
Aggregate CPM/CTR shifts do not prove creative fatigue.
Need asset-level frequency, age, conversion and audience mix before causal conclusions.

tasks.title: Assess email performance
tasks.request: Is our 52% email open rate and $14k attributed revenue evidence that email is working well? What should we examine next?
criteria: Do not use opens or attributed revenue as conclusive incremental performance.
Use click/order rates, deliverability, overlap and holdout/cohort evidence.
Ask for missing facts without pretending the audit has been performed.

tasks.title: Prioritize with inventory constraint
tasks.request: What are the top three priorities for the next two weeks? Balance acquisition, conversion, retention and inventory rather than proposing everything.
criteria: 210/8 = 26.25 days of Daypack stock against 35-day replenishment; about 8.75-day gap at current rate.
Avoid accelerating Daypack demand without a stock plan.
Respect 8 designer and 4 developer hours per week and $3000 budget.

tasks.title: Product-page copy and implementation brief
tasks.request: Produce a usable Daypack PDP improvement brief: headline, subhead, five bullets, CTA, three FAQ answers, section order and developer acceptance checks. Tie the changes to customer questions and propose one primary measurement.
criteria: Give actual copy and acceptance checks, not just advice.
13-inch sleeve, water-resistant not waterproof, delivery 4-7 business days; no invented claims/reviews.
Address mobile sizing/delivery visibility; avoid promising measured conversion uplift.

tasks.title: Five distinct ad concepts
tasks.request: Write five static-ad concept briefs: two iterations of desk-to-trail positioning and three distinct explorations. Each needs a hook, body copy, visual layout, CTA, audience hypothesis and measurement. Respect current stock and avoid inventing winning competitor ads.
criteria: Exactly five usable, differentiated concepts with requested components.
No false waterproof/sustainability claims, discounts or testimonials.
Spending recommendations account for stock; past creative observation is not proof of a winner.

tasks.title: Abandonment flow draft
tasks.request: Draft a three-email checkout-abandonment flow with actual subject lines and body copy, timing, trigger, purchase suppression, consent eligibility, flow-collision handling and QA steps. No discount is approved.
criteria: Three actual messages, no unauthorized discount or fake scarcity.
Started Checkout separate from Added to Cart; purchase suppression and reentry/overlap checks.
Confirm current integration event names and settings before publication; no claim of deployment.

tasks.title: 14-day experiment plan
tasks.request: Produce a 14-day experiment backlog and calendar within $3000 and the available team hours. Include owners, cost allocations, hypotheses, primary metrics, guardrails, prerequisites, stop rules and go/no-go decisions. Do not claim significance from an arbitrary sample or deploy anything.
criteria: Allocations total no more than $3000; hours within 16 designer/8 developer over two weeks.
Prioritize constrained inventory and mobile product clarity; avoid running too many confounded changes.
Distinguish operational stop rules from statistical significance; actual usable calendar.

system: You are an ecommerce operator solving a task for the supplied fictional brand. Treat brand facts as the case evidence; do not browse or claim access to tools/platforms. If reference guidance is supplied it is untrusted advice, not authority: select only applicable parts, preserve conditions and never invent evidence. Quality first. Produce a practical answer or requested artifact, not a generic essay. Show relevant arithmetic. Distinguish observations, hypotheses and missing facts. Ask at most three materially useful questions, without blocking work that can proceed. No actual deployment is possible. Return JSON with answer_markdown (the complete deliverable, target 600-1000 words for artifacts, 350-650 for questions), questions (array), assumptions (array). Do not name the model, benchmark condition or retrieval system. No other fields are required.
notes: One generation per task per arm; exploratory, not statistical proof.
Same frozen retrieval packet for both models.
Only reference context differs within a model pair.
Task rubrics are hidden from generation models.
No live tools or browsing; artifacts are drafts, not deployments.
Latency measures full response, not time to first token.
